name: Skills Tree
description: Branching skill tree that unlocks nodes with earned skill points, gated by level requirements. A run that crosses between regions tears the whole build down and rebuilds it, so anything a player earned has to be handed to the next build through a DECLARED input or it is silently lost — which is how an RPG hands back a fresh character every time you walk off the edge of the map. That is what the initial-state input below is for: it is the same rule economy.currency's startingBalance follows, and it is a request's business to supply, never this component's to remember. A node that unlocks and changes NOTHING is a list of words on a panel, which is what this was: it published names, and no component in any build read one. The fix is not for this component to reach into combat and movement and apply effects — that is the second place a number gets computed, and it would make a progression component a combat component. It publishes `bonuses`, a summed table of the modifiers its unlocked nodes declare, and the components that own those numbers read it. So the CONTENT of a skill lives in the request's treeDefinition where a designer can change it, the summing lives here, and applying it stays with whoever owns the thing being modified. Ranked trees remain the same owner: maxRank defaults to 1 and costByRank defaults to one point per rank, so legacy boolean nodes behave exactly as before. `effect` is a per-rank modifier, which is identical to the old unlock-once result at rank 1. Prerequisites may require a minimum rank in another node, and exclusiveGroup prevents two competing nodes from holding ranks simultaneously. New purchases validate every rule; restored ranks deliberately do not. The tree publishes available and lockedBy for UI and planRespec for dependency-safe refunds, but Build Respec owns cross-system transactions and Ability Loadout owns active-slot selection. Ordinary purchases emit skillRankChanged. A respec instead emits one skillRespecCompleted summary for its transaction id, not another per-rank event storm, so downstream loadout pruning and persistence cannot apply the same rebuild twice. Optional specialization gating extends the same purchase rules without changing legacy trees: a node may declare `specialization`, and specializationGateMode 'whenDeclared' then requires the matching active identity for NEW purchases while restored ranks remain untouched. Selection changes refresh availability and lockedBy only; they never erase ranks or emit a respec. Nodes without the field behave exactly as before, and Build Respec still owns rank refunds.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.
Upstream module named; no adapter written.

inputs.name: treeDefinition
inputs.description: The tree: {startingPoints?, skills: [{id, name, atLevel, maxRank?, costByRank?, prerequisites?, exclusiveGroup?, effect?}]}. Prerequisites are [{id, rank?}] and default to rank 1. maxRank defaults to 1; costByRank defaults to 1 for every rank. `effect` is an optional object of named per-rank modifiers — {meleeDamage: 1} at rank 2 contributes 2 — summed into `bonuses` for the components that own those stats. A node with no effect remains a legal title, prerequisite, or active-ability source.

inputs.name: initialUnlocked
inputs.description: Node ids already unlocked when the build starts. Prerequisites are NOT re-checked against this list: it is a restore, not a purchase, and re-validating it would let a tree edited between sessions silently delete a player's build.

inputs.name: initialRanks
inputs.description: Restored ranks keyed by node id. Takes precedence over initialUnlocked when both name a node. Like the legacy restore, it is not revalidated against a tree that may have changed between sessions; new purchases still validate every rule.

inputs.name: initialPoints
inputs.description: Unspent points at the start. Null means the tree's own starting allowance, which is what a fresh character gets.

inputs.name: specializationGateMode
inputs.description: whenDeclared enforces a node's optional specialization field through progression.specialization.isActive for new purchases; disabled ignores that field for hosts deliberately using tree content without specialization selection. Legacy nodes have no field and are unaffected.

outputs.name: bonuses
outputs.description: Every `effect` on every unlocked node, summed by key — e.g. {meleeDamage: 2, meleeRange: 1}. Read by the components those keys belong to: combat.melee_basic owns reach and the damage it requests, movement.basic_walk owns pace. Additive because two nodes granting the same bonus should stack in the obvious way, and because a designer reading the tree should be able to add the numbers up in their head and get the same answer the game does.

outputs.name: ranks
outputs.description: Current rank per node id; omitted or zero means locked.

outputs.name: available
outputs.description: Nodes whose next rank currently satisfies level, prerequisite, exclusivity, declared specialization, and point-cost rules.

outputs.name: lockedBy
outputs.description: Per unavailable next rank, the concrete missing level, prerequisite ranks, exclusive conflict, inactive specialization, or points.

outputs.name: spentPoints
outputs.description: Points invested in current ranks, before any respec refund.

outputs.name: planRespec
outputs.description: Pure query returning the ranks and refund affected by a full or selected-node respec. rejectDependents refuses a partial plan that orphans dependents; cascadeDependents includes them explicitly.
